approved: Introduced Appropriation Bill (No. 3) 2012-13 seeking $600,797,000 in additional funding, including $85 million for childcare support, $60 million for the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, $37 million for offshore asylum seeker management and $26 million to support Tasmania's health system.
Moved that Appropriation Bill (No. 3) 2012-2013 and Appropriation Bill (No. 4) 2012-2013 be referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

Criticised the appropriation bills as a symbol of government mismanagement amid a $120 billion black hole of unfunded promises, saying the government cannot explain how it will fund the NDIS, dental schemes or Gonski recommendations.

Defended the government's job creation record, saying 840,000 jobs have been created and warned the opposition's proposed $71 billion in cuts would have a $280 billion ripple effect on the economy, and cited his own club's diversification program as an example of local jobs growth.

Reported on Lunar New Year celebrations across his multicultural Fowler electorate, including a Tet festival at Fairfield showground attended by 30,000 people over three days despite heavy rain, and noted more than 30 per cent of his community has an Asian background.

Supported the appropriation bills, highlighted $16.2 billion in Building the Education Revolution investment nationally including over $92 million across 45 schools in his Moreton electorate, and criticised the opposition's proposed cuts to education funding.

Described a delegation to Myanmar observing GAVI vaccination work and argued that its partnership model delivers effective aid, strengthens health systems and saves lives. Reported that GAVI had immunised more than 370 million children and saved more than 5.5 million lives in 72 countries, and supported Australia maintaining its funding commitment.

Argued that government taxation and carbon-tax policies damage Western Australia's mining sector, mismanage mining-tax revenue and threaten investment and jobs. Opposed removing fringe benefits tax exemptions for fly-in fly-out and drive-in drive-out workers, saying these arrangements support resource projects and spread economic benefits.

Questioned the detail and funding basis of an equity injection for Defence under Appropriation Bill (No. 4) 2012-2013, and warned against further reductions to defence spending. Argued that repeated cuts, deferments and absorbed costs had weakened capability, and said the coalition would guarantee no cuts and rebuild the Defence Force.

Supported the appropriation bills, highlighting the transition from GEERS to the legislated Fair Entitlements Guarantee, funding for the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, and an ANSTO nuclear medicine facility at Lucas Heights. Also supported energy-efficiency funding for councils and community organisations, including street-light upgrades.

Argued that the carbon tax increased electricity prices without reducing emissions and disproportionately affected pensioners, low-income families, farmers and small businesses. Reported concerns about carbon-tax advertising and destroyed grant documentation, and called for a full and independent inquiry into the Energy Efficiency Information Grants Program.

Argued that regional students face unfair financial and emotional barriers when relocating for university because the student income-support system counts parental income and provides inadequate assistance. Called for a fairer system, including a tertiary access allowance for students required to move from regional communities.

Argued that the carbon tax and MRRT harmed business, jobs, competitiveness and public finances, citing impacts on industries in Queensland and calling for their abolition. Criticised government spending, debt and defence reductions, while supporting mining investment and warning that Australian industries faced declining productivity and international competition.

Called for construction of an inland rail freight line from Melbourne to Brisbane, saying it would cut the trip to about 20 and a half hours and shorten the route by 170 kilometres compared with the coastal line, at an estimated cost of about $4.7 billion.

Argued that rising costs for electricity, water, gas, education, medical care and childcare were hurting families and were worsened by budget deficits, the carbon tax, taxes and regulation. Proposed removing the carbon tax, reviewing policies, cutting taxes and red tape, and conducting a competition review, particularly into supermarkets.

Argued that Labor's appropriation-funded investments represented a national vision, highlighting around $6.8 billion for Victorian road, rail and public transport infrastructure. Reported commitments including $110 million for education infrastructure, $3.2 million for an Outlook community centre, and $1.5 million for an equine trade training centre.

Argued that the appropriation bills reflected unreliable forecasting, increased offshore asylum seeker costs and a $390 million tax compliance allocation affecting small business. Criticised the carbon tax, proposed funding commitments and private health insurance changes, and supported a plan to restore small business confidence.

Reported regional investments including $5 million for Crown Street Mall, $2.6 million for the Warilla Southern Community Hub and Youth Foyer, and $17.2 million in grants to 25 businesses expected to create 512 jobs. Also highlighted education, health, volunteer and innovation funding across the Illawarra.

Explained that the appropriation bills sought just over $1.27 billion, including approximately $85 million for childcare assistance, approximately $600 million for the royal commission into institutional responses to child sexual abuse, and additional funding for border protection, health, taxation and defence. Praised the government's economic management.

Argued that the steel assistance package compensated for the carbon tax and criticised MYEFO forecasts, the mining tax and borrowing-funded commitments. Reported that a planned Port Augusta drug and alcohol rehabilitation centre had stalled, and called for regional infrastructure including ports, roads, energy and telecommunications.

Argued that government economic management had supported growth, jobs and families, citing an economy 13 per cent larger and more than 850,000 jobs created since Labor took office. Reported Schoolkids Bonus payments to approximately 11,200 families and opposed proposals to restore taxes affecting low-income earners.

Criticised the carbon tax as set to create a $4 billion budget black hole once linked to the European scheme in 2015, said the mining tax had raised only $126 million against a promised $2 billion, and said federal revenue was now more than $90 billion a year higher than in the coalition's last year in office.

Criticised the appropriation bill's extra $37 million for offshore asylum seeker management, said net debt had grown to a whopping $147 billion in five years, and outlined coalition plans including a 15,000 strong green army and a five per cent emissions reduction target by 2020.

Said the two appropriation bills add $1.27 billion in spending, said Queensland health cuts translated to a $3.2 million reduction at Mackay Hospital and $7.8 million at Townsville Hospital, and said the government's debt interest bill of $800,000 an hour could otherwise have funded Bruce Highway projects like the Mackay ring road.
